correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, 1<=w<=n, use piecewise-affine selector matrices. Exact Gini cut coarea reduces every branch to t(n-t)/[k(n-k)]. For 2w<=n, c_j<=w and a two-case scalar inequality prove <=w(n-w)/(n-1); for 2w>=n, the unique global peak wins exactly w rows, forcing every cut image size outside (n-w,w). A one-peak perturbation attains equality, including w=n=zero. The normalization, quotient by constants, boundary cases and n/4 envelope were checked. Exact exhaustive order checks n<=8 and rational pair checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Gini dispersion is an invariant of all pairwise contrasts, a natural alternative to adjacent variation and centered Euclidean error for nonlinear sample pooling. This single theorem settles the sharp two-input stability of every cyclic contiguous max window in every dimension, explains exact first amplification at four sites, and shows linear worst-case growth n/4 despite one-input shape preservation. The proof supplies a reusable sharp occupancy-cut bound and a complementary global-peak obstruction at half-cycle windows; the exact constants are neither a renaming nor a direct specialization of the inspected earlier path-TV or Hilbert results.
